We need to parse the specification. It's about Spring Framework, Spring XD, Admin SPI, Receptor and cloudController implementations, module registry abstraction, profile-aware SPI implementation, Eureka self-registration, search modules by name, store module metadata in Eureka.

User stories:
U1: Use Receptor implementation of Admin SPI for deploying Spring XD modules, query status/health. APIs: getStatus, listModules, map.
U2: Use cloudController implementation of Admin SPI similarly.
U3: Permanent location of SPI implementations (common repo) for contributions/test coverage.
U4: Create initial version of new module registry abstraction, foundation to test SPI implementations (receptor or cloudcontroller).
U5: Make SPI implementation profile aware, so running java -jar admin or cf push admin or ltc create admin wires corresponding implementation automatically.
U6: Modules self-register with Eureka when installed, discover via Spring XD Admin SPI and reuse to create data pipelines.
U7: Search modules by name aside from default spring.application.name, fetch modules by name.
U8: Store module metadata in Eureka, use repository to determine current state.

This is a backend Java/Spring project. We need to implement:
- Define Admin SPI interfaces (ModuleStatus, ModuleDescriptor, etc.) maybe already exist? But U4 says create initial version of new module registry abstraction. U3 says permanent location of SPI implementations (common repo). So we need to set up a module/repo for SPI and implementations.
- Implement Receptor Admin SPI implementation (status, list, map).
- Implement CloudController Admin SPI implementation (same APIs).
- Make SPI implementation profile aware (Spring profiles: default, cloud foundry, local? maybe profile-based bean wiring).
- Module registry abstraction initial version.
- Eureka integration: modules self-register with Eureka, store metadata, search by name, discover via Admin SPI.
- Possibly refactor or extend Admin SPI to support Eureka-based discovery/registry.

We need to break down into activities. Let's think of WBS.

Possible activities:
A1: Set up common repository/module structure for Admin SPI and implementations (U3). Includes build config, package layout, CI maybe.
A2: Define/refine Admin SPI interfaces and core domain types (ModuleDescriptor, ModuleStatus, ModuleRegistry abstraction) (U4, U1/U2 APIs). Actually U4 says create initial version of new module registry abstraction. So design module registry abstraction and Admin SPI.
A3: Implement Receptor Admin SPI implementation (U1). Includes querying Receptor for module status/health, mapping to SPI.
A4: Implement CloudController Admin SPI implementation (U2). Similar for CF cloud controller.
A5: Implement profile-aware SPI wiring (U5). Use Spring profiles to conditionally enable Receptor or CloudController or default. Configuration and auto-configuration.
A6: Implement Eureka integration for module self-registration (U6). Modules register with Eureka on install, including metadata.
A7: Extend/implement module registry abstraction to use Eureka as backend (U8) and support search by name (U7). This includes storing metadata in Eureka, querying by name, and exposing via Admin SPI.
A8: Write unit and integration tests for SPI implementations and Eureka integration, plus test coverage in common repo (U3, U4).
A9: Documentation and example usage? Might be optional. But for software increment, maybe include developer docs and configuration docs. Could be part of activities.

We need to estimate effort in workdays (most likely). We are a single developer doing all work. Need reasonable estimates.

Let's think about scope. This is a fairly complex distributed systems integration with Spring, Eureka, Cloud Foundry, Receptor (probably a CF container networking thing? Actually Receptor is maybe a Spring XD admin SPI for CF?). But we can assume familiarity.

- Use Java 17+ and Spring Framework 6 (as per spec, Spring requires Java 17+). But Spring XD is older? However spec mentions Spring XD on CF, s-c-s (Spring Cloud Services?). We'll assume modern Spring Boot 3 / Spring Cloud for Eureka.
- Use Spring Profiles for profile-aware wiring (U5).
- Use Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka (or Eureka client) for service registration/discovery.
- Admin SPI defined with interfaces: ModuleStatus, ModuleDescriptor, ModuleRegistry (or AdminSPI) with methods getStatus, listModules, etc.
- Create a separate Maven/Gradle module (common repo) for SPI and implementations (U3).
- Receptor and CloudController implementations are Spring beans implementing Admin SPI, activated by profile.
- For Eureka-based module registry, store module metadata as Eureka instance metadata; search by name using Eureka's metadata query or extend discovery client.
- Use dependency injection and auto-configuration.

Assumptions:
- Existing Spring XD codebase is available; we are adding these features as increments, not from scratch.
- Basic Eureka server is available in environment; we only implement client-side registration and discovery.
- Receptor and Cloud Controller APIs are accessible via REST; we assume stable API contracts and credentials provided via config.
- "Permanent location of SPI implementations" means a new dedicated Git repository or module within monorepo; we assume a new Maven module.
- One developer with full stack Spring experience; no external dependencies waiting.

A2: Design and implement Admin SPI and Module Registry abstraction.
Description: Define ModuleDescriptor, ModuleStatus, AdminSpi/ModuleRegistry interfaces (getStatus, listModules, etc.), and initial module registry abstraction to be used by implementations.
Effort: 3 workdays.

A3: Implement Receptor Admin SPI implementation.

Effort: 5 workdays.

A4: Implement CloudController Admin SPI implementation.
Description: Develop CloudController-based implementation of Admin SPI for CF, similar methods, handling CF push deployment, mapping responses.
Effort: 5 workdays.

A5: Profile-aware SPI wiring.
Description: Configure Spring profiles (e.g., "receptor", "cloudcontroller", "local") so that running admin via java -jar, cf push, or ltc create automatically wires the correct implementation using @Profile or auto-configuration.

Effort: 6 workdays.

A9: Documentation and example configuration.
Description: Write developer docs for SPI, how to contribute, profile usage, Eureka metadata schema, and example deployment commands.
Effort: 2 workdays.
